title: Intervariant Tokenization and Context Window Parity: Regeneration & CI Enforcement
creator: Leah Park
description:
Summary:
Maintain and re-generate the intervariant parity matrix focused on tokenizer behavior, context window boundaries, and runtime tooling contracts for fallback model variants. This ticket delivers an automated CI stage and a lightweight regeneration workflow so routing fallbacks can be validated quickly and reliably before being used by Smart Routing policies (region selection/tier routing/fallback decisions).

Background:
Our Smart Routing layer can route requests to fallback variants when primary variants are unavailable or when routing policies prefer lower-cost tiers. Past incidents have shown subtle tokenizer/context mismatches and KV-cache edge cases that produce degraded outputs or runtime errors when requests are redirected. The current parity matrix is partially manual and out of date for several newly onboarded model variants and quantization-targeted builds.

Objectives:
- Regenerate the tokenization/context-window matrix for all production fallback candidates (including quantized variants) and record canonical mismatch categories.
- Implement an automated CI job that runs a prioritized smoke-suite (golden prompts + boundary context cases) against every variant pair that a routing policy may route between. The job should fail on behavioral regressions or desync exceptions.
- Add runtime lint checks to the model onboarding toolchain to surface tokenization divergences and KV-cache contract mismatches earlier.
- Produce a small remediation playbook for the routing team: when the CI flags a mismatch, how to triage (tokenizer normalization, adapter patches, or routing blacklist).

Acceptance criteria:
1) A regenerated parity matrix (CSV + human-readable summary) uploaded to the model-catalog bucket, covering all variants used in routing policies.
2) CI job (pipeline name: variant-parity-smoke) that runs for each merge to main on model-adapter changes and model catalog updates. The pipeline must produce a machine-readable report and a top-level pass/fail status visible in PRs.
3) A modeled set of 120 golden prompts covering prefix edge cases, long-context truncation, rare unicode handling, and KV-cache warm/hot path scenarios. The smoke-suite detects at least the three classes of mismatches we defined: token id drift, context-offset shifts, and KV-cache token boundary regressions.
4) Runtime onboarding linter integrated into the model adapter CLI that fails local builds if tokenization hashes differ beyond tolerance thresholds.
5) Documentation: short runbook for routing owners + an FAQ explaining how CI failures map to routing decisions and safe rollout steps.

Technical approach and plan:
- Phase 1 (3 days): Inventory all fallback variant pairs referenced by Smart Routing policies (region/tier lists + fallback matrix). Export tokenizer vocab checksums and context-window metadata.
- Phase 2 (4 days): Build the smoke-suite harness that executes tokenization => encode/decode roundtrips, injects KV-cache warm sequences, and compares model behavior signals (log-prob distribution shifts for anchor examples).
- Phase 3 (5 days): Implement the CI job in the existing infra (buildkite -> mutable runner pool), wire artifact publishing to model-catalog, and add PR gating.
- Phase 4 (2 days): Add model-adapter CLI linter entry point and document the tolerances and remediation steps.
- Phase 5 (1 day): Run a full sweep, triage top 5 mismatches, and produce the runbook.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Conservative failure threshold is preferred for high-risk routes (enterprise customers) and can be relaxed for low-tier fallbacks if risk-tolerance policy allows. We'll expose that as a routing-policy flag.
- Running the full smoke-suite against all variants is expensive; the CI will prioritize pairs that are actually referenced by routing maps, and incremental runs will use sample-based checks.
- Some mismatches will require upstream tokenizer fixes (model repo) — we will include guidance but not own that repo changes.

Risks:
- False positives in CI due to nondeterministic sampling; mitigate with seeded runs and stable anchors.
- Slow CI runtime impacting developer velocity; mitigate with parallel runners and early short-circuit for gross mismatches.

Deliverables:
- matrix: sources/model-catalog/intervariant_parity_2026-03-12.csv
- CI job: buildkite pipeline variant-parity-smoke and PR status integration
- linter: model-adapter CLI subcommand parity-check
- runbook: docs/routing/fallback-parity-runbook.md

Longer-term ideas (beyond this ticket):
- Add telemetry gating to runtime routing so that degraded outputs trigger automatic temporary blacklist of a variant pair until remediation.
- GPU-side microbenchmarks for quantized variants to identify when performance vs. parity tradeoffs are causing drift.
